title: The signature-request operations exist in no P5 source and carry no API ID, because the legacy key is a communications module story while the table is P5's
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 Appendix T-A.1 (API-P5-001 to API-P5-017, no signature path) and T2; FSD P5 Document hub v3 (no e-signature or signature section); Ownership rows of the P5 context pack (signature_request owned by P5); legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 1, 12 and 13
section: Section 1 Story, section 3 Preconditions, 12.1 REST operations provided, 12.8 Contract fakes, section 13 Solution plan
description: The endpoint inventory of rwb-document holds seventeen document operations and none of the three signature endpoints of legacy RWB-E2-018, and the functional specification of the module has no e-signature section at all, because the legacy key is a P6 Communications story. The table route_index places signature_request with P5, so the request has to be created, read and updated in rwb-document, and the five operations this story needs therefore have no API ID, no documented path, no query names and no element names in any source. The story serves them on base /api/recovery/document/v1 with the legacy section 12 shapes rebased per DP-13, names the absence in the table and in this row, and keeps API-P5-005 as the only published operation it provides. No path, query or field name is invented as a settled value: each is marked as not specified in the source documents and faked until the API Specification carries it.
evidence: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T-A.1 rows API-P5-001 POST /cases/{caseId}/documents through API-P5-017 POST /documents/{documentId}/regenerate, with no signature operation; FSD P5 Document hub v3 section list with no e-signature section; context pack Ownership rows tables (12) including signature_request; legacy RWB-E2-018 section 12 endpoint table and section 13 component table.
proposed: Add the five signature-request operations to TSD P5 Appendix T-A.1 with their API IDs and to the API Specification at its next version, with the paths of this story, and settle the query names of the list and the external-reference read with rwb-comms in the same review

title: signature_request is defined in TSD P6 T3.1 inside the communications module and owned by P5 in the ownership ruling, so the table has no P5 data model
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (signature_request defined) and T2; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 (no signature_request row); Ownership rows of the P5 context pack (signature_request listed among the 12 P5 tables); Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 11 and 13
section: Section 1 Story, section 3 Preconditions, section 11 Data, 12.7 Tables owned, section 13 Database and migrations
description: Two sources place the same table in different services: the technical specification of rwb-comms declares signature_request with the legacy field list, and the ownership rows of the P5 context pack list it among the twelve tables rwb-document owns, as the Architecture v5 catalogue slides do. The service facts of the context pack are the authority for ownership, so the table is P5's and rwb-comms holds none; but rwb-document has no data model for it, no column list, no constraint and no index in its own technical specification. The story therefore creates the table in schema rwb_document from the legacy field list DF-DOC-096 to DF-DOC-107, with the unique index on external_ref, the index on (treatment_id, status) and the check constraint on method and status, and records that the P5 data model has to catch up at its next version.
evidence: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 signature_request rows with DF-DOC-096 to DF-DOC-107; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 object list without signature_request; context pack Ownership rows Tables (12) with signature_request; legacy RWB-E2-018 section 11 table and section 13 database note.
proposed: Keep signature_request in rwb_document as the ownership ruling states, remove it from the rwb-comms data model at the next version of TSD P6, and add the table with its constraints and indexes to TSD P5 T3.1 and to the Physical Schema file rwb_document.sql

title: The platform contracts and the P3 reference-data contract that the nine applied patterns add are absent from this story's build and contract rows, which the Work Package fixes as empty
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP table; Work Package B2-P5-006 story line for RWB-P5-E2018-APP (H [], C [], I [], X []); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17, 20 and 43; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.2 (lists of values)
section: Metadata table (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies), section 3 Preconditions, 12.2 REST consumed, section 13 Pattern application
description: Five of the nine patterns this story applies add a dependency row in the DP table: DP-07 adds the platform reference-data library and the rwb-case reference-data contract, DP-09 the outbox and inbox library, DP-10 the workflow kit, DP-15 the per-service Flyway sequence and DP-19 the gateway-bff composite route. The Work Package gives the story four empty dependency lists, so the story cannot state its build dependency and would otherwise claim a Day-1 start with no library and no contract named. The story keeps the four rows exactly as the Work Package fixes them, names the five platform CONs and the one P3 contract in the pattern table and in the preconditions, builds against their fakes on Day 1, and records the gap here rather than adding rows to the plan.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-07 (H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON), DP-09 (H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), DP-10 (H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), DP-15 (H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON), DP-19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON); Work Package B2-P5-006 story line with H [], C [], I [] and X []; Architecture v5 slide 20 (gateway-bff one hop, 2 s, breaker) and slide 43 (outbox and inbox per service).
proposed: Record the six platform CONs as wave-0 platform release train prerequisites of every wave-1 service and add RWB-P3-E1043-CON to the contract rows of the stories whose pattern set claims DP-07, so the dependency map shows the real graph without deepening lane L-P5-W

title: No source names a signature event on the rwb-document topic, and the request state is readable only through the operations of the story
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T5.3 (DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted published) and the context pack Events (EV-16, EV-17); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 4 and 12
section: Section 4 Flow step 11, 12.3 Events published, 12.4 Events consumed, 12.9 Call-type summary
description: The legacy story raised CUSTOMER_SIGNED in P3 and had no event of its own for a signature. In the target, the catalogue of this service names two events only, DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted, and no source gives rwb-document a signature event, a payload or a topic name. A new event cannot be invented without a payload contract, an AsyncAPI document and a consumer, so the story publishes DocumentStored from the version add, exactly as any stored document is published, and publishes no signature event: the request state is read by its callers through the five operations. The consequence is stated in the story so that no consumer waits for an event that does not exist, and any later push to rwb-reporting or rwb-case is a new story with DP-09 and the platform event library.
evidence: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T5.3 table with DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted published; context pack Events (2) EV-16 and EV-17; Architecture v5 slide 42 (events of rwb-document); legacy RWB-E2-018 section 4 step 6 (CUSTOMER_SIGNED raised in P3) and section 12 (no published event).
proposed: Accept DocumentStored as the only event of this story and settle with rwb-reporting whether a signature fact is needed on the topic; if it is, allocate it as a new story with DP-09, a CloudEvents payload of IDs and facts only, and no personal data

title: The write-once container, the WORM tier, the size limit and the byte transfer behind the signed-version add are named by no source
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T-A.2 (the API-P5-005 entry) and T7 (NFR-069, NFR-029); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 8 (Blob WORM, documents); legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 4, 12 and 13
section: Section 3 Preconditions, section 4 Flow step 6, 12.1 REST provided (API-P5-005), 12.8 Contract fakes, 12.9 Call-type summary, section 17 Guardrails
description: The signed PDF reaches this service as the bytes of a version add, and the store that holds it must be write-once inside the retention period. The sources fix the requirement and the container family - Blob with WORM, about 2.8 TB by the end of 2031 - but no source names the container, the tier, the maximum object size, the transfer path of the bytes or the way the write-once refusal is reported, and the non-functional table leaves the retention periods open. The story therefore builds the version add on API-P5-005, keeps the write-once flag and the version chain as the guarantee it can test, and stubs the container in the contract fakes, with the boundary values recorded here rather than guessed in code.
evidence: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T-A.2 API-P5-005 entry; T7 rows NFR-069 (2.8 TB by 2031) and NFR-029 (write-once for legal types); Architecture v5 slide 8 (Blob WORM, documents); legacy RWB-E2-018 section 13 (new version of the agreement) and section 12 (addVersion with the signed PDF).
proposed: Settle the container, the WORM tier, the object size limit and the transfer path of a signed PDF with the store story RWB-P5-E1024-APP and the infrastructure story of the service, and carry them as configuration rows of rwb.document.esign rather than as constants

title: No rwb-document message exists for a closed signature request and no source names the operation-level right of the five request operations
source: Legacy RWB-E2-018 section 14 (MSG-P3-005 used for a request that is not open) and section 12 (Treatment and offer rights); TSD P5 Document hub v2 T6.1 (Documents column only) and T-A.1 (Documents C, R, U per operation); legacy section 16 TC-E2-018-12
section: Section 10 Authority, 12.1 REST operations provided, section 14 Validation and messages, section 16 Test cases
description: Two values of the story have no owner document. First, the refusal of a result on a request that is already SIGNED, DECLINED or EXPIRED: the legacy story reused MSG-P3-005, a rwb-case message about a case that cannot move to a state, and no rwb-document message exists for a closed request; the story keeps MSG-P3-005 unchanged so the legacy test text still holds and records that a message of the owning service is owed. Second, the right each of the five operations declares: the legacy story names Treatment and offer rights, which are rwb-treatment's and rwb-case's area, while TSD P5 T6.1 declares only the Documents column, so the story declares Documents C, R and U per operation and proves the refusal with the role row RW-PHONECOL, which holds Documents R only.
evidence: legacy RWB-E2-018 section 14 row MSG-P3-005 and section 12 Authorization column (Treatment and offer C, R and U); TSD P5 Document hub v2 T6.1 rows RW-RESTRUCT Documents CRU, RW-CASEOWN CRU, RW-LEGAL CRUA, RW-PHONECOL R; legacy RWB-E2-018 section 16 TC-E2-018-12.
proposed: Keep MSG-P3-005 as the closed-request refusal for this version and add a rwb-document message at the next version of the message standard, and confirm Documents C, R and U as the operation-level rights of the signature-request operations in the RBAC matrix
